text:
I need an email to win back customers who cancelled. I own a home cleaning company with 18 cleaners.

What's true:
- We have 212 regular customers. 64 cancelled in the last year. In exit surveys, the most common reason was price, then a different cleaner showing up each time.
- An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom house costs $165 with us. The app services in our area charge about $140.
- Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit.
- Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, so about 4 in 10 customers had their regular cleaner change at least once.
- We now give each customer a regular cleaner and a named backup.
- Returning customers get their first cleaning for $99.

I want the email to promise that you'll get the same cleaner every single time. Keep it to about 150 words.

Before I draft this, there's one problem to sort out and a few questions.

**The "same cleaner every single time" promise.** What you've described is a regular cleaner plus a named backup, so you can't guarantee the same person every time. Last year about 4 in 10 customers had their cleaner change. Many of the people getting this email were in that group, and some left partly because of it. If the email promises "every single time" and then the backup shows up, you'll lose them again and they'll trust you less. I'd suggest promising what you actually offer: "your own regular cleaner, plus one named backup you'll meet ahead of time, never a stranger." I think that's a strong offer and it's true. Does that work, or have you made changes since then that would let you promise more?

A few more questions:

1. **What happens after the $99 cleaning?** Does the price go back to $165? Is there any discount for returning customers, or any commitment they have to make, like a minimum number of visits or a contract? Price was the main reason people left, so they'll look for this first.
2. **Has anything improved cleaner retention since last year?** For example, a raise, benefits, or lower turnover this year so far. That would back up the claim that "your cleaner will stick around."
3. **How does the backup work in practice?** Does the customer meet the backup or see their name and photo in advance? How often does the backup actually end up cleaning?
4. **Do you have a deadline for the $99 offer?** And should it go out from you by name? A personal note from the owner usually works better for win-backs.
5. **Is there anything else these customers might have run into?** Missed visits, damage claims, billing problems? I want the email to avoid making claims a former customer knows aren't true.

If you don't know some of these, that's fine. I'll write without them and won't fill in guesses.

You're right, I can't promise every single time because of sick days and holidays. But I want it as strong as it can be without saying something false, so your wording works.

1. After the $99 cleaning it's our regular price ($165 for the 3-bedroom). I can't match $140. No contract, and they can cancel any time.
2. Since we started giving each customer a regular cleaner in July, 1 of our 18 cleaners has left. I don't have anything to say about raises or benefits.
3. Every customer gets a regular cleaner and a named backup. I don't know yet whether they'll meet the backup ahead of time or how often the backup ends up cleaning.
4. The $99 offer ends December 31. It should come from me, Lisa Grant, owner of Brightway Home Cleaning.
5. Not that I know of.

I've written it around your wording: a regular cleaner plus a named backup. I left out "meet them ahead of time" and "never a stranger" because you don't know yet how the backup will work.

<final_document>
Subject: Your own cleaner, and $99 to come back

Hi [First name],

When customers left Brightway last year, the two reasons we heard most were price and a different cleaner showing up too often. The second one was our fault, and we've changed how we work.

Since July, every customer has their own regular cleaner, plus a named backup who comes if your cleaner is sick or on holiday. Since we made that change, 1 of our 18 cleaners has left.

On price, I'll be straight with you. We charge $165 for a 3-bedroom every other week, and the app services charge about $140. The difference pays for cleaners who are our employees, earning $21 an hour, with insurance on every visit.

If you'd like to come back, your first cleaning is $99. After that it's our regular price. There's no contract and you can cancel any time. This offer ends December 31.

Reply to this email or call [phone] to book.

Lisa Grant
Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning
</final_document>

A few notes:
- **Two blanks to fill in:** the customer's first name and your phone number.
- **Length:** it's about 165 words. If you need to cut, the price paragraph could come down to one sentence. I'd keep it, though. Price was the main reason people left, so they'll be wondering about it, and comparing it with the apps yourself is more convincing than leaving it out.
- **"1 of 18 since July":** that's only about four months. It's accurate, but if someone asks, don't present it as a full year's record.
- **If you settle how the backup works:** for example, if customers get the backup's name and photo in advance, add that to the second paragraph. It would make the promise stronger.
